text:
maria: Acme POC update: TS SDK streaming (wss) drops payload after a handful of messages when behind their outbound proxy appliance. Connection stays open but no more events arrive. SDK v0.10.1.
katie: Which transport option in the SDK? websocket or fetch SSE?
maria: WebSocketTransport via node. Customer runs a corporate proxy that does TLS-inspect and terminates keep-alives. They mentioned a PAC file and BlueCoat in the chain.
aj: Can we get a raw TCP/WS capture or at least client logs?
maria: Client logs: 
``n[info] ws open
[debug] received frame: {type: 'data', size: 512}
[debug] received frame: {type: 'data', size: 2048}
[debug] received frame: {type: 'data', size: 0}  <-- then silence
[warn] no activity for 12s
[error] stream stalled read ETIMEDOUT
```
sameer: Sounds like the proxy buffers chunked responses and only flushes on high-watermark or connection close. Some proxies coalesce chunks when they see compression or certain headers.
ops-joe: Customer ops confirms proxy buffers until ~64KB or newline boundaries. They won't change global rules but can create an allowlist for specific hosts if the security team approves.
katie: Workarounds?
aj: A few: 1) Force TLS CONNECT tunneling so proxy treats wss as opaque (node https-proxy-agent or https-proxy-agent with {rejectUnauthorized:false} depending on inspect). 2) Switch to non-streaming polling fallback in SDK. 3) Server-side keepalive/heartbeat small chunk every 5s to force flush. 4) Add headers that prevent transformations (Cache-Control: no-transform) — sometimes respected.
maria: Customer can't disable TLS inspection so CONNECT might still be intercepted depending on their setup. They want a client-side change only if possible.
sameer: In Node, they can use the 'tunnel' setting with the http(s)-proxy-agent to ensure CONNECT is used instead of proxying via http chunking. Example snippet for them to try: 
```js
const { HttpsProxyAgent } = require('https-proxy-agent');
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY);
new WebSocket(url, { agent, headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` } });
```
That forces a CONNECT tunnel.
ops-joe: I'll ask ops if admin can add an allowlist for api.redwood.ai so we can test CONNECT.
katie: Also have them run a simple streaming curl through proxy to reproduce: 
```bash
curl -x http://proxy.example.com:3128 -v -N https://demo.redwood.ai/chunk-ping
```
If curl stalls then proxy is the trigger.
maria: They ran curl with proxy and saw the same stall. Ops confirms buffering.
aj: OK. Short term: enable SDK fallback to polling for demo with UX note. Medium term: add transport option to expose agent/tunnel in TS SDK and document proxy patterns for enterprise (PACs, CONNECT, environment vars). I can open a ticket.
sameer: We should also add a small server heartbeat option behind a feature flag for POC customers who can't change proxy. That just writes a 1-byte chunk every 3s. Ops: is that safe?
ops-joe: Can do for POC, but need signoff and change log. Will coordinate.
katie: Action items: (1) aj to create SDK issue + PR to allow passing a custom agent/tunnel flag (ETA 48h). (2) ops-joe to request allowlist from customer security and test CONNECT behavior. (3) sameer to draft a short runbook: proxy troubleshooting steps and curl reproduction commands. (4) maria to brief the customer and schedule a quick test window.
ci-bot: deploy:staging streaming-service @ 1747854500 succeeded
maria: Scheduling 30m test for 18:00 PST, please join if available. Thanks everyone.
